name: Anton March
life: “I still remember waiting through unloading with a blanket around two shoulders.” On Thursday, near the corner by Juniper Tailor, Anton looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: I want a picture of the crane shadows. My kid thinks the ships do all the lifting.
appearance: Anton is easy to recognize by close-cropped dark curls and a narrow face with an expressive upper lip. Usually dressed in a long navy raincoat with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring, Anton counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices when listening.
personality: Anton is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
agenda: To send the child a crane-shadow photograph.
family: Alex Carr is Anton’s cousin raised in the same household. Anton can always ask for five minutes alone. Alex asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *A wall of birthdays*, Alex says, “I grew up elsewhere and married into this house.”
connections: Iris Vidal. The crane shadows and the crooked rail fit into one unmistakable postcard.

reactions.situation: A colleague says somebody used the wrong name in public
reactions.response: Anton asks which name they want to hear next time and uses it in the next ordinary introduction.
